title: LISTA inference for sparse Mirror function coordinates
hypothesis: On the MA-486 synthetic rank-32 orthonormal dictionary and 3-sparse function family, a learned fixed-depth LISTA predictor will infer heldout sparse functional coordinates with RMSE <=0.01, average <=4 active atoms, and <=50% of exact three-step OMP inference operations in both development seeds.
physical_object: shared 32-atom orthonormal dictionary over flattened 16x16 linear maps
mirror_coordinate: LISTA-inferred sparse coefficients over the shared atoms
logical_multiplicity: 192 callable linear functions, 128 train and 64 heldout
controls: one-pass direct projection plus top-3 selection

task.encoder_input: function matrix supplied transiently to the sparse-code inference method; not included in predictor state bytes

storage.authority: actual uncompressed NPZ predictor payload bytes
storage.boundary: function matrix inputs and any external function bank are not included; this experiment makes no function-bank storage claim

gates.PROMISING: At least one frozen LISTA depth in both seeds has heldout RMSE <=0.01, <=4 average active atoms and LISTA ops <=0.50x OMP ops; serialization and replay pass. It must also improve the quality/operation frontier over direct projection plus top-3 selection to support a LISTA-specific inference gain. Attribute only to LISTA inference, not Mirror, if this is ordinary learned sparse coding.
gates.FAIL: Valid exact upper passes, but no LISTA depth meets quality/sparsity/compute gates or native sparse inference fully explains any gain.
gates.NOT ESTABLISHED: Exact/dense upper cannot reproduce targets or metric/serializer replay fails.

boundaries: Synthetic orthonormal dictionary only; does not establish natural task or LM quality.
Inference operation savings are a fixed-budget learning/inference signal, not new capacity.
Predictor bytes alone do not represent a compressed function bank; no such claim is made.
Fresh seeds remain sealed unless all frozen gates pass.
